title: Closures Check
description: Predict how closures capture and mutate private state across factory calls.

options.text: A function bundled with references to variables from its creation scope
A copy of all global variables made at function definition time
A special syntax for defining classes
A way to prevent a function from being called twice

questions.explanation: A closure is a function paired with references to the variables from the scope where it was created, even after that scope has returned.
`count` starts at 5 and each `inc()` call mutates the same closed-over variable, ending at 7.
Each call to the factory function creates a fresh, independent closure. Mutating `a`'s `count` never affects `b`'s `count`.

questions.prompt: Why can't outside code read `count` directly in the counter example?

options.text: Because `count` is declared with `let` inside the factory and never exposed on the returned object
Because JavaScript objects cannot have numeric properties
It actually can be read directly; closures don't provide privacy

questions.explanation: `count` only exists inside the factory's scope. The only access paths are the methods (`inc`, `dec`, `get`) that the factory chooses to return.

questions.prompt: Does a closure capture a snapshot (value) or a live reference to its outer variable?

options.text: A snapshot taken at the moment the closure is created
A live reference — later mutations to the variable are visible inside the closure
Neither — closures cannot access outer variables at all
It depends on whether the variable is a primitive or an object

questions.explanation: Closures capture variables by reference. If the outer variable changes after the closure is created, the closure sees the updated value.
First call flips `on` from `false` to `true` (returns `true`, discarded). Second call flips it back to `false` and returns `false`.
